set.rappels: One 60 m rope reaches only the first rappel (about 15 m); below that, walk off to the west or traverse to the 3rd-class ramp
set.rappel_count_note: The rappel line down this wall has four stations of about 15, 55, 50 and 40 m, and the three lower ones are too long for a single 60 m rope. No intermediate anchors are known for one rope, so a party with one rope should not plan to rappel the line. The first rappel, about 15 m from a slung tree at the top, trending slightly left to a larger tree, is within one rope. For the rest, walk off to the west down 3rd-class terrain, or traverse off to the 3rd-class ramp partway down. Nearly every anchor below the top trees is bolted, and some rappels are diagonal.
set.descent_text: From the top, walk down the 3rd-class terrain to the west, or traverse to the 3rd-class ramp partway down. The Ellen Pea rappel line below the top trees uses stations too long for one 60 m rope (diagonal rappelling is required in places).

rappel_detail.station: The slung tree at the top of the route.
rappel_detail.notes: About 15 m, trending slightly left to a larger tree. Below this, the documented stations are too long for one 60 m rope.

set.rappels: No single-rope rappel line is known; with one rope, top out and scramble off down and left on a treed ramp
set.rappel_count_note: The rappel line down the route has seven stations of about 30 to 61 m, and most are too long for a single 60 m rope. No intermediate anchors for one rope are known. With one rope, top out and scramble down and left on a treed ramp into the 3rd-class gully left of the wall. From the base, walk left down the gully, or rappel the bolted slab below and right: about 75 m more, on three bolted anchors.

set.rappel_count_note: Parties describe between one and three short rappels on the forested upper East Ridge, with brush belays or downclimbing between them, so the count depends on conditions and how much is downclimbed. Each station listed is about 30 m, within one 60 m rope.

set.rappels: 2 rappels are documented, from near the summit to the Middle-South Gunsight notch and into the moat below it; the length of each is unknown, so whether one 60 m rope reaches is not established
set.rappel_count_note: Parties describe one rappel from the south-facing anchors near the summit to the notch between Middle and South Gunsight, then one more, loose, dirty and cold, into the moat at the base of the notch. No source gives a length for either, and no single-rope line with intermediate stations is known. Do not assume one 60 m rope reaches; check each drop before committing.

set.rappels: No single-rope descent is documented; the known descent is 2 rappels down the West Face, separated by belayed downclimbing of the summit ridge and several hundred feet of Class 3 on the dike
set.rappel_count_note: A four-station sequence of 50/50/50/20 m is sometimes attached to this route. It matches, figure for figure, the descent of north Gunsight Peak's West Face, a 5.11+, 6-pitch, 600 ft rock route on a different summit, and does not belong to this Class 5.6 glacier route on the main spire. Nothing about those figures was measured here, so they are not carried. The documented descent is two rappels: after belaying back down the exposed summit ridge, one rappel down the west face, then a diagonal rappel, with directional protection placed along the way, that reaches the snow finger in one go. Both are long, and no intermediate anchors are known, so it is not established that a single 60 m rope does either.
set.descent_text: Reverse the ridge crest from the summit: belay/downclimb the exposed summit ridge back down to a large horn about 50' below the true summit that is thickly slung with rappel webbing (a good on-route confirmation marker). From there, rappel the West Face to regain the base of the route's black basaltic dike/dihedral. Scramble down several hundred feet of Class 3 terrain on the dike to the top of the crux dihedral, then make a second, diagonal rappel — the last person down should place a directional piece of protection to keep the rope running true — which in one pull reaches the snow finger below. From the snow finger, downclimb or glissade back onto the Chikamin Glacier and reverse the approach (re-climb to the Chikamin-Dome col, cross the Dome Glacier, over Itswoot Pass/Cub Pass, down Bachelor Meadows/Bachelor Creek, and out Downey Creek Trail #768) to the trailhead. All anchors reported on this route are natural — slung horns, blocks, and chockstones — with no fixed/bolted stations, consistent with its remote, low-traffic character. Expect the crux dihedral's black rock to be loose in spots, and factor in real crevasse-travel time and daylight for the long glacier return to camp.

review.single_rope: No single-rope descent documented; the two rappels are long and have no stated lengths or intermediate anchors.

No source gives a length for either, and no single-rope line with intermediate stations is known. Do not assume one 60 m rope reaches; check each drop before committing.
set.descent_text: From the summit, traverse south along the summit ridge to the south-facing rappel anchors and make two rappels: the first to the notch between Middle and South Gunsight, the second into the moat at the base of the notch (loose, dirty and cold). No single-rope count is documented. From the glacier, reverse the approach: descend roughly 5,000 ft back to Agnes Creek and hike out 9-10 miles to High Bridge.

set.rappels: 4-5 rappels on a single 60 m rope; one lower rappel is overhanging
set.rappel_count_note: Parties report four to five rappels on one 60 m rope: a rappel from a ledge just below the summit, a single-rope rappel from the bottom of the shoulder to the top of pitch 2, then the overhanging drop to below Gunsight Notch in two rappels. The count differs by party depending on where the rappelling starts and how much is downclimbed. Anchors are natural slings and cord; parties report adding cord to one and rebuilding another.
set.descent_text: Descend by reversing the final scramble pitches/downclimbing back to the top of the technical face (the uppermost section is a downclimb/scramble to the top of the East Face), then begin a rappel sequence rather than trying to downclimb the buttress itself — the rock is loose enough that down-climbing the route is not recommended. From a small ledge/anchor on the east side just below the summit, a rappel gets you down the steepest upper wall (rockfall-prone — the next rappeller should move off to the side immediately, not straight down, to avoid anyone above). Below that, from the bottom of the shoulder, one rappel on a single 60 m rope reaches the belay station at the top of the second climbing pitch. From there the line drops over an overhanging section to just below the north side of Gunsight Notch in two rappels on a single 60 m rope. Anchors are fixed natural slings and cord rather than bolts, and parties regularly add cord or rebuild one, so carry some. Move off the fall line as soon as you are down each rappel; rockfall knocked loose by the party above is a recognized hazard here. Below the notch, re-descend the glacier and snowfield and Mixup Arm to Cascade Pass.
